senses.gloss:
Airāvata, ‘son of Irāvant,’ is the patronymic of dhṛtarāṣṭra, as a snake demon, in the Atharvaveda and the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes In the later literature airāvata is the elephant of indra: perhaps connected with this Vedic snake demon. as nāga means both ‘serpent’ and ‘elephant.’
viii. 10, 29.
xxv. 15, 3.
